diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑api latency spiked from ~200 ms to 2150 ms immediately after the 10:15 PM deployment of v4.17, causing connection‑pool timeouts and upstream 504 errors.
diagnosis.root_cause: The release changed orders‑client v3 which reconfigured the database pool to max_connections=10 and acquire_timeout_ms=2000, exhausting the pool and blocking checkout requests.

evidence.finding: Deployment DEP-88213 of checkout‑api v4.17 started at 10:15 and finished at 10:17:40
p95 latency jumped from 200 ms to 2150 ms within minutes of the deployment
orders‑db pool max=10, in_use=10, waiting=143, acquire_wait_p95_ms=1800, timeouts_per_min=212
Error logs show ConnectionPoolTimeoutError with 2000 ms timeout and 504 upstream errors
Slow trace shows db.pool.acquire taking 1829 ms as the dominant span

ruled_out: Increased traffic volume – latency spike aligns exactly with deployment time, not a gradual trend.
External orders‑db outage – logs show only pool exhaustion errors, no connectivity failures.

proposal.rationale: The latency spike correlates exactly with the 10:15 PM deployment of v4.17, which introduced a reduced orders‑db connection pool (max_connections=10, acquire_timeout_ms=2000). Pool exhaustion caused ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and upstream 504s, driving p95 latency to ~2150 ms. Rolling back to the previous stable release v4.16 restores the original pool configuration and is the safest remediation.
